page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is configured with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware configuration includes 1229 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, while containing no GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing it in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and PassMark, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only small block cached speed of 1028.62 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds are 43.86 GB/sec and 26.01 GB/sec respectively. Data processing benchmarks, including gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, consistently align with average tier performance.

The high memory density relative to compute resources makes this instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads such as relational databases, in-memory caching systems, and large-scale data analytics. The inclusion of 1229 GB of local SSD storage supports applications requiring fast temporary storage, though the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy machine learning training. For inference, the system achieves average speeds, processing 33.92 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B parameter model.
